narrative.overview: Two people talk in a garden; beneath them, the roots of what they're building glow. Threads is the instrument that makes those roots visible without trampling the garden. Warm paper light overhead, near-black ink for what's said, and a single amber glow that marks the moment a connection is found. Ideas are growing things here, not boxes in a dashboard: the graph starts as a few macro shapes and is fanned open on demand, accumulating across sessions rather than arriving all at once. The system is calm by doctrine, not by accident (ADR-011): during a live conversation the interface must recede; motion is slow and low-amplitude, color is held in reserve, and nothing competes with the people talking. Density is reached through navigation. The reference in feel is sublime.app: a quiet, beautiful tool for thought, warm and unhurried rather than clinical. It explicitly rejects the cluttered expert tool that shows everything at once, and the loud or gamified app with bright palettes and attention-grabbing motion.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground, near-black ink, one amber accent held in reserve.
A cool spectral hierarchy carries meaning in the graph (teal -> blue -> indigo -> purple -> slate).
Calm, low-amplitude motion; the tool never competes with the conversation.
Drill-don't-dump: highest tier first, detail on demand.
Provenance is visible — amber marks the exact utterance behind any claim.

rules.name: The One Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber is the only warm accent and appears on a small fraction of any screen — a highlight, one CTA, one active chip. If two amber things compete for the eye on the same surface, one is wrong.

rules.name: The Meaning-Is-In-The-Graph Rule
rules.body: Saturated hue is reserved for the graph's semantic tiers and edges. Chrome stays paper / ink / one accent. A colorful sidebar steals the signal the graph needs.

rules.name: The Wordmark-Only Tracking Rule
rules.body: The -0.09em crush is reserved for the 'Threads' wordmark. Everything else stays at or above -0.04em so letters never touch.

rules.name: The One-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: The uppercase tracked label is a single brand gesture (the wordmark kicker), not a per-section habit.

rules.name: The Flat-On-Paper Rule
rules.body: A surface gets a shadow only because it floats over the canvas. If it's part of the page, it's flat. No resting drop-shadows on cards or the graph.

dos: Do keep chrome on paper / ink / one amber accent. Saturated hue belongs to the graph.
Do default to the highest tier of structure and let the user fan into detail — drill, don't dump. Breathing room is a feature.
Do pair every semantic graph color with a line-style or label, so meaning survives without hue (color-blind safe by construction).
Do keep motion slow and low-amplitude. Every animation needs a prefers-reduced-motion alternative.
Do use amber as the single signal of 'a connection / the current line / the one CTA'.
Do lift a surface with shadow only when it genuinely floats over the canvas.
donts: Don't make it cluttered or dense-to-a-fault — no wall of chips, no everything-visible canvas, no expert-tool-that's-hostile-to-read.
Don't make it loud, gamified, or playful — no bright saturated palettes, badges, confetti, streaks, or attention-grabbing motion (ADR-011).
Don't drift into the generic SaaS-dashboard look (gradient hero-metrics, endless identical card grids) or the cold sterile enterprise-admin feel.
Don't use a colored side-stripe border (border-left > 1px as an accent). Panel edges are 1px hairlines.
Don't use gradient text or decorative glassmorphism. The paper gradient and the occasional backdrop-blur on Home are the deliberate exceptions; keep glass rare.
Don't stamp the uppercase tracked eyebrow above every section, or crush tracking past -0.04em anywhere but the 'Threads' wordmark.
Don't add a second warm accent or let two amber elements compete on one surface.
